q: Put these mountains in order by height.
fact: Everest's official height of 8,848.86 m was agreed jointly by China and Nepal in 2020, after both countries measured it.

q: Put these rivers in order by length.
fact: River lengths vary by source, so these are about figures. The Nile flows through 11 countries on its way to the Mediterranean.

q: Put these oceans in order by area.
fact: The Pacific is larger than all of Earth's land put together.

q: Put these continents in order by area.
fact: Asia, missing here, is the biggest of all at about 44.6 million km2 - nearly a third of Earth's land.

q: Put these continents in order by population.
fact: Africa has the youngest population of any continent - about half of its people are under 20.

q: Put these deserts in order by area.
fact: A desert is defined by how little rain or snow falls, not by heat - so icy Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth.

q: Put these islands in order by area.
fact: Borneo is the only island shared by three countries: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

q: Put these lakes in order by surface area.
fact: Areas are approximate. Baikal is modest in area, but it is so deep that it holds about a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water on Earth's surface.

q: Put these lakes in order by maximum depth.
fact: Baikal's surface is 456 m above sea level, so its deepest point lies about 1,186 m below sea level.

q: Put these volcanoes in order by height.
fact: Etna's height changes with its eruptions - surveys since 2021 have put its summit between about 3,350 and 3,400 m, so its figure is approximate.

q: Put these landmarks in order by height.
fact: For about 3,800 years the Great Pyramid was the tallest structure ever built by people.

q: Put these Summer Olympics host cities in order by the year they hosted.
fact: Each of these cities has hosted the Summer Games exactly once. Rio 2016 was the first Olympics in South America.

q: Put these countries in order by when they first hosted the FIFA World Cup.
fact: The United States hosted again in 2026, sharing the first 48-team World Cup with Canada and Mexico.

q: Put these inventions in order by when they appeared.
fact: The first powered airplane flight, by the Wright brothers in 1903, lasted just 12 seconds.

q: Put these landmarks in order by the year they opened.
fact: The Empire State Building went up in about 410 days, opening in 1931 during the Great Depression.

q: Put these languages in order by number of native speakers.
fact: Counting second-language speakers too, English has the most speakers in the world - about 1.5 billion.

q: Put these countries in order by area.
fact: Russia stretches across 11 time zones, from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific Ocean.

q: Put these countries in order by population.
fact: India overtook China as the most populous country in the world in 2023, according to UN estimates.

q: Put these countries in order by number of land neighbors.
fact: China and Russia tie for the most land neighbors in the world, with 14 each. Portugal's only neighbor is Spain.

q: Put these universities in order by founding year.
fact: Bologna, still teaching after more than 900 years, is usually called the oldest university in the Western world.

q: Put these landmarks in order by when they were completed.
fact: The dates for Angkor Wat and Machu Picchu are approximate; Machu Picchu was built for the Inca ruler Pachacuti around 1450.

q: Put these sporting events in order by the year they were first held.
fact: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world. The first one, in 1877, had 22 players - all men.

q: Put these currencies in order by when they were introduced.
fact: The euro began as an electronic currency in 1999; the coins and notes arrived in 2002.

q: Put these countries in order by size of their economy (GDP).
fact: These are rounded IMF estimates for 2026. Measured by purchasing power instead of exchange rates, China's economy is already the largest in the world.

q: Put these foods in order by when they were invented.
fact: Instant noodles were invented in Japan by Momofuku Ando. The world now eats more than 100 billion servings a year.

q: Put these chili peppers in order by heat.
fact: Heat is measured in Scoville units. The Carolina Reaper was the world's hottest pepper until Pepper X took the record in 2023.

q: Put these countries in order by population density.
fact: Mongolia is the most thinly populated country in the world, with only about two people per square km.

q: Put these countries in order by number of official languages named in their constitution or national law.
fact: Bolivia's constitution recognizes Spanish and 36 indigenous languages, including Quechua, Aymara and Guarani. Zimbabwe's lists 16, among them sign language.

q: Put these countries in order by number of states or provinces, not counting territories or capital districts.
fact: Australia, Nigeria and the US all keep their capital outside the states, in a federal territory or district.

q: Put these alphabets in order by number of letters.
fact: Italian uses only 21 letters - j, k, w, x and y appear only in words borrowed from other languages.

q: Put these novels in order by year of publication.
fact: One Hundred Years of Solitude, by Colombia's Gabriel Garcia Marquez, has sold about 50 million copies.

q: Put these painters in order by year of birth.
fact: Van Gogh sold very few paintings in his lifetime, yet he made about 860 oil paintings in barely ten years.

q: Put these countries in order by the year their national anthem became official.
fact: South Africa's anthem uses five of its languages: Xhosa, Zulu, Sesotho, Afrikaans and English.

q: Put these flags in order by number of stars.
fact: Brazil's 27 stars show the night sky over Rio de Janeiro on the morning the republic was declared in 1889.

q: Put these flags in order by number of stripes.
fact: Greece's nine stripes are said to match the nine syllables of the Greek motto 'Freedom or Death'.

q: Put these countries in order by the year their current flag was adopted.
fact: Canada's maple leaf flag replaced the Red Ensign in 1965 after a long national debate over the design.

q: Put these events in order by year.
fact: The first modern Olympics, in Athens in 1896, had about 240 athletes from 14 nations.

q: Put these space milestones in order by year.
fact: The International Space Station has had people aboard without a break since November 2000.

q: Put these countries in order by when women won the right to vote nationally.
fact: In 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing country where women could vote in national elections.

q: Put these explorations in order by year.
fact: Of Magellan's five ships, only the Victoria made it home to Spain in 1522, with Juan Sebastian Elcano in command.

q: Put these countries in order by length of coastline.
fact: Coastlines are hard to measure - the more detailed the map, the longer they get. These are CIA World Factbook figures.

q: Put these countries in order by the height of their highest point.
fact: Denali in Alaska rises about 5,500 m from its base - a bigger base-to-summit rise than Everest's.

q: Put these places in order by elevation.
fact: All four lie below sea level; the Dead Sea and Caspian figures are approximate. The Dead Sea is shrinking by about a meter a year, so its shore keeps getting lower.

q: Put these continents in order by number of countries.
fact: Africa has more countries than any other continent - 54 recognized by the United Nations.

q: Put these cities in order by elevation.
fact: La Paz is the highest seat of government in the world; Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional capital.

q: Put these countries in order by when they first hosted the Winter Olympics.
fact: Beijing is the only city to have hosted both the Summer Olympics (2008) and the Winter Olympics (2022).

q: Put these countries in order by when they first hosted the Summer Olympics.
fact: Stockholm 1912 was the first Olympics to use electronic timing and a public address system.

q: Put these countries in order by Rugby World Cup titles.
fact: South Africa won back-to-back titles in 2019 and 2023, and has never lost a Rugby World Cup final.

q: Put these countries in order by men's Cricket World Cup titles.
fact: Australia won its sixth title in 2023, beating hosts India in the final in Ahmedabad.

q: Put these countries in order by coffee production.
fact: Brazil has been the world's biggest coffee grower since the 1800s. A standard bag of coffee beans weighs 60 kg.

q: Put these countries in order by tea production.
fact: Kenya grows less tea than India but sells most of its crop abroad, making it one of the world's biggest tea exporters.

q: Put these European mountains in order by height.
fact: Elbrus, in Russia's Caucasus Mountains, is a dormant volcano and is usually counted as the highest peak in Europe.

q: Put these European rivers in order by length.
fact: Lengths are approximate. The Danube flows through or along 10 countries - more than any other river in the world.

q: Put these European lakes in order by area.
fact: Lake Ladoga, near St Petersburg, is the largest lake entirely in Europe. Vanern in Sweden is the largest in the EU.

q: Put these European islands in order by area.
fact: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea.

q: Put these European countries in order by area.
fact: France is the largest country in the European Union, even before counting its overseas regions.

q: Put these European countries in order by population.
fact: Almost half of the people who work in Luxembourg commute in every day from France, Belgium and Germany.

q: Put these Nordic countries in order by population.
fact: About two out of every three Icelanders live in and around the capital, Reykjavik.

q: Put these capitals in order by latitude.
fact: Reykjavik in Iceland is the northernmost capital of a sovereign country, at about 64 degrees north.

q: Put these Italian cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Rome is also one of the largest cities in Europe by area: about 1,285 square km, including plenty of farmland.

q: Put these German cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Hamburg, a port city full of canals and rivers, has about 2,500 bridges - around six times as many as Venice.

q: Put these Spanish cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Madrid sits near the center of Spain at about 650 m above sea level, one of the highest capitals in Europe.

q: Put these French cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Lyon's wider metro area is bigger than Marseille's, but within city limits Marseille comes first. It was founded by Greek sailors around 600 BC.

q: Put these UK cities in order by population of their council area (for London, Greater London).
fact: Birmingham, in the middle of England, has more km of canals than Venice.

q: Put these European landmarks in order by when they were completed.
fact: The Atomium in Brussels was built for the 1958 World's Fair and shows an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

q: Put these European landmarks in order by height.
fact: Lakhta Center in St Petersburg is the tallest building in Europe. Cologne Cathedral was the world's tallest building from 1880 to 1884.

q: Put these composers in order by year of birth.
fact: Mozart wrote his first pieces at the age of five and composed more than 600 works in his short life.

q: Put these countries in order by when they joined the European Economic Community or the European Union.
fact: France was one of the six founding members of the European Economic Community, which began in 1958.

q: Put these countries in order by when they adopted the euro.
fact: Bulgaria became the 21st country to use the euro on 1 January 2026.

q: Put these tunnels in order by length.
fact: The Gotthard Base Tunnel under the Swiss Alps, opened in 2016, is the longest railway tunnel in the world. Norway's Laerdal is the longest road tunnel.

q: Put these European countries in order by the height of their highest point.
fact: Switzerland's highest peak, the Dufourspitze, stands in the Monte Rosa massif right next to the border with Italy.

q: Put these Nordic capitals in order by founding year.
fact: These are the traditional dates. Copenhagen grew around Bishop Absalon's castle of 1167. Helsinki was founded in 1550 by King Gustav I of Sweden as a trading rival to Tallinn.

q: Put these countries in order by men's European Championship football titles.
fact: Spain's fourth title came in 2024, making it the most successful team in the tournament's history.

q: Put these Greek islands in order by area.
fact: Greece has about 6,000 islands and islets, but only around 200 of them are inhabited.

q: Put these Asian mountains in order by height.
fact: Damavand in Iran is the highest volcano in Asia. Mount Apo is the highest peak in the Philippines.

q: Put these Asian rivers in order by length.
fact: Lengths vary by source. The Yangtze is the longest river in the world that flows entirely within one country.

q: Put these Asian islands in order by area.
fact: Java is the most populous island on Earth, home to more than 150 million people.

q: Put these Asian lakes in order by area.
fact: Lake Balkhash in Kazakhstan is fresh water in its western half and salty in its eastern half.

q: Put these Asian countries in order by area.
fact: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.

q: Put these Asian countries in order by population.
fact: Almost half of Mongolia's people live in the capital, Ulaanbaatar.

q: Put these Middle Eastern countries in order by area.
fact: Saudi Arabia is the largest country in the world without a single permanent river.

q: Put these Asian capitals in order by latitude.
fact: Singapore lies only about 140 km north of the equator, while Ulaanbaatar is the coldest capital in the world.

q: Put these Asian landmarks in order by when they were completed.
fact: At 634 m, Tokyo Skytree is the tallest tower in the world.

q: Put these skyscrapers in order by height.
fact: The Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 until Taipei 101 passed them in 2004.

q: Put these Japanese imperial eras in order by when they began.
fact: Showa, lasting more than 62 years, is the longest era in Japan's history.

q: Put these Chinese dynasties in order by when they began.
fact: The Qing was China's last imperial dynasty; it ended in 1912. The Ming built most of the Great Wall we see today.

q: Put these Japanese cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Tokyo's figure is the whole Tokyo Metropolis. Yokohama is Japan's second-largest city, even though it sits only about 30 km from central Tokyo.

q: Put these Japanese islands in order by area.
fact: Honshu is the seventh largest island in the world and home to Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto.

q: Put these Indian states in order by area.
fact: Goa is India's smallest state, while Rajasthan, home to most of the Thar Desert, is the largest.

q: Put these Turkish cities in order by population of their whole province.
fact: Istanbul is split between Europe and Asia by the Bosporus strait, with about two thirds of its people on the European side.

q: Put these Asian countries in order by year of independence.
fact: Iraq left British rule in 1932. Singapore became independent when it separated from Malaysia in 1965, and Brunei left British protection in 1984.

q: Put these African mountains in order by height.
fact: Mount Stanley in the Rwenzori Mountains still has glaciers, even though it lies almost on the equator.

q: Put these African rivers in order by length.
fact: Lengths are approximate. The Congo is the deepest river in the world, with places more than 220 m deep.

q: Put these African lakes in order by area.
fact: Lake areas change with the seasons, so these are about figures. Lake Tana in Ethiopia is the source of the Blue Nile.

q: Put these African countries in order by area.
fact: Algeria is the largest country in Africa, and more than four fifths of it lies in the Sahara.

q: Put these African countries in order by population.
fact: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa - roughly one in every six or seven Africans is Nigerian.

q: Put these African capitals in order by latitude.
fact: Nairobi lies just south of the equator, but at about 1,800 m up it has mild weather all year.

q: Put these African landmarks in order by when they were completed.
fact: The Great Mosque of Djenne in Mali is the largest mud-brick building in the world, and the townspeople replaster it every year.

q: Put these African countries in order by year of independence.
fact: Ghana was one of the first colonies south of the Sahara to win independence, in 1957.

q: Put these African deserts in order by area.
fact: The Namib is thought to be the oldest desert in the world, dry for at least 55 million years.

q: Put these Egyptian cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Alexandria was founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC and was home to the most famous library of the ancient world.

q: Put these Moroccan cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Rabat is Morocco's capital, but Casablanca is its biggest city and business center. Figures are from the 2024 census.

q: Put these South African cities in order by founding year.
fact: Johannesburg grew from a gold-mining camp in 1886 into South Africa's largest city in only a few decades.

q: Put these African waterfalls in order by height.
fact: Victoria Falls is not the tallest, but at about 1.7 km wide it is often called the largest sheet of falling water in the world.

q: Put these African islands in order by area.
fact: Madagascar split from India about 88 million years ago, and most of its animals and plants live nowhere else.

q: Put these countries in order by their first FIFA World Cup appearance.
fact: Egypt was the first African team at a World Cup. In 2022 Morocco became the first African team to reach a semifinal.

q: Put these African countries in order by the height of their highest point.
fact: Egypt's highest peak, Mount Catherine in Sinai, rises above St Catherine's Monastery, which has stood for about 1,500 years.

q: Put these mountains of the Americas in order by height.
fact: Because Earth bulges at the equator, Chimborazo's summit in Ecuador is the point on land farthest from Earth's center.

q: Put these countries of the Americas in order by the height of their highest point.
fact: Brazil's highest peak, Pico da Neblina, means 'Peak of the Mist' because it is almost always in cloud.

q: Put these rivers of the Americas in order by length.
fact: Lengths are approximate. The Amazon carries more water than any other river - about a fifth of all river water reaching the oceans.

q: Put these Great Lakes in order by area.
fact: Lake Michigan is the only one of the five Great Lakes that lies entirely within the United States.

q: Put these islands of the Americas in order by area.
fact: Hispaniola is shared by two countries, Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

q: Put these countries of the Americas in order by area.
fact: Chile stretches about 4,300 km from north to south but is on average only about 177 km wide.

q: Put these countries of the Americas in order by population.
fact: Mexico has more Spanish speakers than any other country in the world.

q: Put these Caribbean countries in order by population.
fact: Most of the Bahamas' 700 or so islands are uninhabited; about three quarters of its people live on New Providence, home to Nassau.

q: Put these capitals of the Americas in order by latitude.
fact: In winter, Ottawa's Rideau Canal becomes a skating rink about 7.8 km long that people use to get to work.

q: Put these US cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: New York City is made up of five boroughs: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Staten Island.

q: Put these Brazilian cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Figures are from Brazil's 2022 census. Sao Paulo is the largest city in the Southern Hemisphere.

q: Put these Mexican cities in order by population within city limits.
fact: Cancun was planned by the Mexican government around 1970 on a nearly empty strip of sand.

q: Put these cities of the Americas in order by founding year.
fact: Santo Domingo is the oldest European-founded city in the Americas that is still inhabited.

q: Put these landmarks of the Americas in order by completion year.
fact: Brasilia was built from scratch in about four years to move Brazil's capital inland from Rio de Janeiro.

q: Put these skyscrapers of the Americas in order by height.
fact: Heights are official architectural heights: spires count, antennas do not. One World Trade Center's 1,776 feet recall the year of US independence.

q: Put these countries of the Americas in order by year of independence.
fact: Haiti became the first independent country in Latin America and the Caribbean in 1804.

q: Put these deserts of the Americas in order by area.
fact: Areas are approximate. Death Valley in the Mojave holds the official record for the highest air temperature ever measured: 56.7 degrees C, in 1913.

q: Put these US states in order by when they joined the Union.
fact: Delaware calls itself 'The First State' because it was the first to approve the US Constitution, in 1787.

q: Put these US states in order by area.
fact: Alaska is bigger than Texas, California and Montana combined.

q: Put these Canadian provinces and territories in order by area.
fact: Nunavut, created in 1999, covers about a fifth of Canada but is home to only about 40,000 people.

q: Put these countries in order by Copa America titles.
fact: The Copa America, first held in 1916, is the oldest continental football championship in the world.

q: Put these waterfalls in order by height.
fact: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world - so high that much of its water turns to mist before it lands.

q: Put these mountains of Oceania in order by height.
fact: Aoraki / Mount Cook has shrunk: a huge rockfall in 1991 and erosion since have taken about 40 m off its summit.

q: Put these rivers of Oceania in order by length.
fact: Lengths are approximate. The Waikato is New Zealand's longest river, flowing out of Lake Taupo to the Tasman Sea.

q: Put these islands of Oceania in order by area.
fact: New Guinea is the second largest island in the world, after Greenland.

q: Put these countries of Oceania in order by area.
fact: Tuvalu is made up of nine small islands with a total land area of only about 26 square km.

q: Put these countries of Oceania in order by population.
fact: Nauru, with about 12,000 people, is one of the least populous countries in the world.

q: Put these capitals of Oceania in order by latitude.
fact: Wellington is the southernmost capital of a sovereign country in the world.

q: Put these Australian cities in order by founding year.
fact: Canberra was chosen as a compromise because neither Sydney nor Melbourne would accept the other as the capital.

q: Put these Australian cities in order by population of the greater city area.
fact: Perth is one of the most isolated big cities in the world - Adelaide, the nearest, is more than 2,000 km away.

q: Put these Australian deserts in order by area.
fact: These are Geoscience Australia figures. About 18 percent of mainland Australia is classed as desert.

q: Put these landmarks of Oceania in order by completion year.
fact: Melbourne's Royal Exhibition Building became the first building in Australia to be named a UNESCO World Heritage Site, in 2004.

q: Put these Pacific countries in order by year of independence.
fact: Samoa, independent in 1962, was the first Pacific island country to gain independence in the 20th century.

q: Put these events in New Zealand's history in order by year.
fact: Wellington replaced Auckland as the capital in 1865 because it was more central between the North and South Islands.

q: Put these events in Australian history in order by year.
fact: On 1 January 1901 six British colonies joined together to form the Commonwealth of Australia.

q: Put these Australian states in order by area.
fact: Western Australia covers about a third of the continent - more than three times the size of Texas.

q: Put these New Zealand cities in order by population of the urban area.
fact: About a third of all New Zealanders live in Auckland.

q: Put these New Zealand lakes in order by area.
fact: Lake Taupo fills a huge crater left by a supervolcano eruption about 25,500 years ago.

q: Put these sports in order by when they joined the Summer Olympics.
fact: Judo was added for the Tokyo 1964 Games, the first Olympics held in Asia.

q: Put these cities in order by when their metro system opened.
fact: London's Underground, opened in 1863, was the world's first underground railway - its first trains were pulled by steam engines.

q: Put these European languages in order by number of native speakers.
fact: German is the most widely spoken native language in the European Union - it is official in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Luxembourg and Liechtenstein.

q: Put these Asian countries in order by when they first hosted the Summer Olympics.
fact: Tokyo hosted the Summer Games twice, in 1964 and 2021 - the second time a year late, as Tokyo 2020.

q: Put these countries in order by when their current capital took over as capital.
fact: Australia's parliament moved from Melbourne to Canberra in 1927; Nigeria moved its capital from Lagos to Abuja in 1991.
